# Library and Data

```{r setup}
library(tma)

data(package = "tma", "test_reddit")
reddit_data <- test_reddit;
```

# Prepare Data

```{r data-prep}
# Create a new ID column that concatenates the ID of the original comment to the beginning
reddit_data$ID <- c(reddit_data$structure[1], paste0(reddit_data$structure[1], "_", reddit_data$structure[seq(from = 2, nrow(reddit_data))])) 

# Now we can remove the trailing `_[:digit:]` to get the reference to the parentID, as you suggested
reddit_data$parentID = gsub(x = reddit_data$ID, pattern = "_\\d*$", replacement = "", perl = TRUE)

# Force the original comment's parent to empty
reddit_data[1, "parentID"] <- "";

# Converting to data.table - tma functions will do the coercion anyway, and then we 
# can store a vector of parents in a column (see below)
reddit_data <- data.table::as.data.table(reddit_data);

# tma will require a column for context, forcing all rows to be the same
reddit_data$Context <- "Public";

# create a new column that cont
reddit_data$parents <-lapply(reddit_data$ID, function(smp) {
  pat <- "([^_]+)"
  matches <- regmatches(x = smp, gregexpr(pattern = pat, text = smp, perl = TRUE))[[1]];
  s <- sapply(
    split(sequence(seq(length(matches))), rep(seq(length(matches)), seq(length(matches)))),
    function(x) {
      paste(matches[x], collapse = "_" )
    }
  );
  s
})
```

# Model Prep

```{r model-prep}
# Model Setup ----
reddit_code_cols <- c("Economy","Spread","LetsOpen","TooSoon","politics")
reddit_units_by <- c("user");
test_window_size <- 4;
simple_window <- function(x) { (x < test_window_size) * 1 }
reddit_weight_fun <- function(x) { x };
reddit_hoo_rules <- rules(
  (ID %in% unlist(UNIT$parents))
);
reddit_split_fun <- function(unit, unit_context) {
  unit_rows <- unit_context[unit, c("user", "ID", "parentID", "parents"), on = names(unit)]
  split(
    unit_rows[, {
      res2 <- unit_context[ID %chin% unlist(.SD$parents), ];
      res2$TMA_GROUP <- .GRP
      res2
    }, by = seq(nrow(unit_rows))], 
  by = "TMA_GROUP")
}
```

# Model 1: With Siblings

```{r model-siblings}
reddit_model <- units(reddit_data, by = reddit_units_by);
reddit_model <- contexts(
  reddit_model,
  reddit_hoo_rules,
  split_rules = eval(reddit_split_fun)
)
reddit_model <- accumulate_contexts(
  x = reddit_model, 
  codes = reddit_code_cols,
  weight.by = reddit_weight_fun,
  return.ena.set = TRUE,
  decay.function = simple_window,
  mode.column = 'Context',
  meta.data = c('user')
)
```

To create an ENA model from this accumulation:

```
reddit_model <- rENA::ena.make.set(reddit_model)
```

# Model 2: Model 1 again, but with tma()

```{r model-siblings-tma}
reddit_model2 <- tma(
  data = reddit_data,
  units.by = reddit_units_by,
  hoo.rules = reddit_hoo_rules,
  split.rules = reddit_split_fun,
  code.cols = reddit_code_cols,
  weight.by = reddit_weight_fun,
  return.ena.set = TRUE,
  decay.function = simple_window,
  mode.column = 'Context',
  meta.data = c('user')
)
reddit_model2 <- rENA::ena.make.set(reddit_model2)
```

The output from `tma()` is the same above, in Model 1, so creating the ENA model is the same:

```
reddit_model2 <- rENA::ena.make.set(reddit_model2)
```
